question: Pens are bought by a shopkeeper at the rate of ₹1,200 for 150 pens and sold at the rate of ₹1,620 for 180 pens. His profit or loss percent is
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

The rate of 1 pens, CP = Rs.8

The rate of 1 pens, SP = Rs.9

Profit = 9 - 8 = Rs.1

Profit% = (1/8) × 100 = 12.5** **

**Hence, The profit is 12.5%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of 150 pens = Rs. 1200

Selling price of 180 pens = 1620

**Formula used:**

Profit% = (Profit/Cost price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Cost price of 150 pens = Rs. 1200

Cost price of 1 pen = 1200/150 = Rs. 8

Selling price of 180 pens = 1620

Selling price of 1 pen = 1620/180 = Rs. 9

So, profit = 9 - 8 = Rs. 1 

Profit% = (1/8) × 100 = 12.5

**∴ Required answer is 12.5% profit.**
